column1: # QIAseq 16S/ITS Screening Panel -- region definitions
# PRIMER PROVENANCE
#   fwd_seq / rev_seq are the PHASE-0 (core) primers extracted from QIAGEN's own
#   demultiplexer primer file:
#       16S_primers_ScreeningPanel_Demultiplex_Final.txt.expanded
#   shipped inside the official docker image qiaseq/qiaseq-16s (see reference/ and
#   README "Primer provenance"). That file lists all 12 phase variants (0-11) of
#   every primer with degenerate bases pre-expanded; we collapsed the expansions
#   back to IUPAC and kept phase 0. Phase N is simply N extra bases prepended to
#   the phase-0 sequence, so an UNANCHORED cutadapt 5' match against phase 0
#   removes the phasing bases and the primer in one step, for all 12 phases.
# amplicon_bp  approximate full amplicon length incl. primers (E. coli 16S numbering);
#              NA for ITS1, which is genuinely variable (~230-450 bp).
# trunclenf/trunclenr  DADA2 truncation, passed to ampliseq --trunclenf/--trunclenr.
#              Sized for this run's 2x276 bp reads. Budget per read is
#              276 - 11 (max phasing) - primer_len, and trunclenf+trunclenr must
#              exceed the primer-to-primer insert by >=20 bp for DADA2 to merge.
#              Use the literal value "auto" to let ampliseq pick by quality
#              (--trunc_qmin) instead of a fixed length.
#              >>> These are starting values. After the first run, check
#              <region>/dada2/QC/*.pdf and overall_summary.tsv and retune. <<<
# ref_taxonomy      value for ampliseq --dada_ref_taxonomy
# trim_readthrough  yes = extra cutadapt pass removing the 3' opposite primer
#                   (only needed when the amplicon is shorter than the read)
# extra_args        extra ampliseq flags for this region ("-" for none)
